theory.intro: In an **annuity due**, payments are made at the **beginning** of each period and interest compounds at the end of each period. Start with a zero balance before the first payment and calculate the future value at the **end of the nth period**.
facts: The first deposit compounds for $n$ full periods to $a(1+r)^{n}$, while the final deposit compounds for $1$ period to $a(1+r)$.
The payment series $a(1+r)+a(1+r)^2+\dots+a(1+r)^n$ has first term $a(1+r)$ and common ratio $1+r$. Factoring out $a(1+r)$ leaves $1+(1+r)+\dots+(1+r)^{n-1}$, whose first term is $1$.
For $r\ne0$, summing the derived geometric series gives $FV = a(1+r)\left[\dfrac{(1+r)^{n}-1}{r}\right]$.

For positive payments and a positive interest rate, an annuity due accumulates more interest than an ordinary annuity with identical payments, rates and valuation dates. At zero interest, both have value $na$; use this sum directly because the displayed formula divides by $r$.

Derive the payment series for each problem rather than merely substitute into a memorised annuity formula. Keep full precision until the final rounding. In the solutions, $\operatorname{round}(x,2)$ means round $x$ to the nearest cent.
steps: Identify $a$, the interest rate per period $r$, and the number of periods $n$. Check the payment dates and the valuation date.
Write the series of terms starting from $a(1+r)$ up to $a(1+r)^{n}$, checking that there are $n$ payments and that the final payment earns one period of interest.
Identify the first term and common ratio, derive the geometric-series sum, then evaluate using full precision and round as requested.

workedExamples.question_text: An account contains $\$0$ before the first payment. A deposit of $\$a$ is made at the beginning of each year for $n$ years. Interest at rate $r$ per annum compounds annually. Derive the future value at the end of year $n$, for $r\ne0$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
The first deposit earns $n$ years of interest and the final deposit earns one year.
$FV=a(1+r)^n+a(1+r)^{n-1}+\cdots+a(1+r)$.
In increasing-power order, the series has first term $a(1+r)$, common ratio $1+r$ and $n$ terms.
$\begin{aligned} FV&=a(1+r)\left[1+(1+r)+\cdots+(1+r)^{n-1}\right]\\&=a(1+r)\frac{(1+r)^n-1}{(1+r)-1}\\&=a(1+r)\frac{(1+r)^n-1}{r}.\end{aligned}$
If $r=0$, the deposits earn no interest and $FV=na$.

workedExamples.question_text:
A saver deposits $\$2400$ on 1 January each year for seven years into an initially empty account earning $6\%$ p.a. compounded annually.
(a) Derive a geometric-series expression and calculate the balance at the end of the seventh year, to the nearest cent.
(b) Calculate the value of the first deposit at that date, to the nearest dollar.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) The seven deposits earn seven, six, …, one years of interest.
$FV=2400(1.06)^7+2400(1.06)^6+\cdots+2400(1.06)$.
In increasing-power order, the first term is $2400(1.06)$, the common ratio is $1.06$ and there are seven terms.
$\begin{aligned} FV&=2400(1.06)\left[1+1.06+\cdots+1.06^6\right]\\&=\frac{2400(1.06)(1.06^7-1)}{1.06-1}\\&\approx\$21\,353.92.\end{aligned}$
(b) The first deposit earns seven full years of interest.
$\begin{aligned} V&=2400(1.06)^7\\&\approx\$3609\quad\text{(nearest dollar)}.\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: Priya deposits $\$320$ at the beginning of each month for three years into an initially empty account earning $6\%$ p.a. compounded monthly. Derive a geometric-series expression and calculate the balance at the end of the three years, to the nearest cent.
workedExamples.solution_text:
The monthly interest rate is $r=0.06/12=0.005$, and there are $n=3\times12=36$ deposits.
The first deposit earns 36 months of interest and the final deposit earns one month.
$FV=320(1.005)^{36}+320(1.005)^{35}+\cdots+320(1.005)$.
In increasing-power order, the first term is $320(1.005)$, the common ratio is $1.005$ and there are 36 terms.
$\begin{aligned} FV&=320(1.005)\left[1+1.005+\cdots+1.005^{35}\right]\\&=\frac{320(1.005)(1.005^{36}-1)}{0.005}\\&\approx\$12\,650.49.\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: A club wants $\$30\,000$ at the end of five years. It will make equal deposits at the beginning of each month into an initially empty account earning $7.2\%$ p.a. compounded monthly. Derive a geometric-series equation and find the required monthly deposit, to the nearest cent.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Let the monthly deposit be $M$. The monthly rate is $r=0.072/12=0.006$, and there are $n=5\times12=60$ deposits.
The first deposit earns 60 months of interest and the final deposit earns one month.
$30000=M(1.006)^{60}+M(1.006)^{59}+\cdots+M(1.006)$.
In increasing-power order, the first term is $M(1.006)$, the common ratio is $1.006$ and there are 60 terms.
$\begin{aligned} 30000&=M(1.006)\left[1+1.006+\cdots+1.006^{59}\right]\\30000&=\frac{M(1.006)(1.006^{60}-1)}{0.006}\\M&=\frac{30000(0.006)}{1.006(1.006^{60}-1)}\\M&\approx\$414.38.\end{aligned}$
Keep the accumulation factor unrounded. Rounding the deposit to cents can make the final balance slightly different from the exact target.

foundation.question_text:
A deposit of $\$1000$ is made at the beginning of each year for $5\text{ years}$ into an account earning $7\%$ p.a. compounded annually.
Write the future value as a geometric series and calculate the balance at the end of $5\text{ years}$, to the nearest cent.
foundation.solution_text:
1. **Identify $a$, the interest rate per period $r$, and the number of periods $n$. Check the payment dates and the valuation date.**
$a = 1000$, $r = 0.07$, $n = 5$
There are five start-of-year payments. At the end of year 5, they have earned between one and five years of interest.
2. **Write the series of terms starting from $a(1+r)$ up to $a(1+r)^{n}$, checking that there are $n$ payments and that the final payment earns one period of interest.**
$FV = 1000(1.07) + 1000(1.07)^{2} + 1000(1.07)^{3} + 1000(1.07)^{4} + 1000(1.07)^{5}$
$= 1000(1.07)[1 + 1.07 + 1.07^{2} + 1.07^{3} + 1.07^{4}]$
3. **Identify the first term and common ratio, derive the geometric-series sum, then evaluate using full precision and round as requested.**
The payment series has first term $1000(1.07)$, common ratio $1.07$ and five terms.
$FV = \dfrac{1000(1.07)(1.07^{5}-1)}{0.07}$
$\approx \$6153.29$

foundation.question_text: An account initially contains $\$0$ before the first deposit. There are $n$ start-of-year deposits of $\$a$, and interest at rate $r$ per annum compounds annually. Show that, for $r\ne0$, the future value at the end of year $n$ is $FV = a(1+r)\left[\dfrac{(1+r)^{n}-1}{r}\right]$.
foundation.solution_text:
1. **Write the series of terms starting from $a(1+r)$ up to $a(1+r)^{n}$, checking that there are $n$ payments and that the final payment earns one period of interest.**
Take the initial balance as zero and value the account at the end of year $n$.
First deposit grows for $n$ years: $a(1+r)^{n}$
Last deposit grows for $1$ year: $a(1+r)$
$FV = a(1+r) + a(1+r)^{2} + \dots + a(1+r)^{n}$
2. **Identify the first term and common ratio, derive the geometric-series sum, then evaluate using full precision and round as requested.**
First term is $a(1+r)$, common ratio is $1+r$, number of terms is $n$.
For $r\ne0$, $FV = \dfrac{a(1+r)((1+r)^{n}-1)}{(1+r)-1}$
$= a(1+r)\left[\dfrac{(1+r)^{n}-1}{r}\right]$.
If $r=0$, each of the $n$ terms equals $a$, so $FV=na$.

foundation.question_text:
A parent deposits $\$2000$ at the beginning of each year for $8\text{ years}$ into a college fund earning $5\%$ p.a. compounded annually.
Find the future value at the end of the $8\text{ years}$, to the nearest cent.
foundation.solution_text:
$a = 2000$, $r = 0.05$, $n = 8$.
The eight payments earn between one and eight years of interest.
$FV=2000(1.05)+2000(1.05)^2+\dots+2000(1.05)^8$.
This is a geometric series with first term $2000(1.05)$, common ratio $1.05$ and eight terms.
$FV=\dfrac{2000(1.05)(1.05^8-1)}{1.05-1}$
$\approx\$20053.13$.

foundation.question_text:
James contributes $\$300$ at the beginning of each month for $4\text{ years}$ into a savings plan paying $6\%$ p.a. compounded monthly.
Calculate the value of the investment at the end of the $4\text{ years}$, to the nearest cent.
foundation.solution_text:
$a = 300$, $r = \dfrac{0.06}{12} = 0.005$, $n = 4 \times 12 = 48$.
There are 48 monthly payments; the first earns 48 months of interest and the final payment earns one month.
$FV=300(1.005)+300(1.005)^2+\dots+300(1.005)^{48}$.
The geometric series has first term $300(1.005)$, common ratio $1.005$ and 48 terms.
$FV=\dfrac{300(1.005)(1.005^{48}-1)}{0.005}$
$\approx\$16\,310.22$.

foundation.question_text:
Sophia needs $\$12\,000$ in $3\text{ years}$ for a vehicle purchase.
She will make deposits at the beginning of each month into an account paying $4.8\%$ p.a. compounded monthly.
Find the required monthly deposit, to the nearest cent.
foundation.solution_text:
$r = \dfrac{0.048}{12} = 0.004$, $n = 36$.
Let the monthly deposit be $a$. At the end of month 36, the 36 payments have earned between one and 36 months of interest.
$12000=a(1.004)+a(1.004)^2+\dots+a(1.004)^{36}$.
The geometric series has first term $a(1.004)$ and common ratio $1.004$.
$12000=a\dfrac{1.004(1.004^{36}-1)}{0.004}$.
The exact accumulation factor is $\dfrac{1.004(1.004^{36}-1)}{0.004}$; retain this value rather than rounding the factor.
The monthly deposit to the nearest cent is $\$309.34$.

foundation.question_text:
A saver deposits $\$1600$ at the beginning of each year for $3\text{ years}$ into an account earning $5\%$ p.a. compounded annually.
Calculate the balance at the end of the $3\text{ years}$, to the nearest cent.
foundation.solution_text:
The three deposits earn three, two and one years of interest respectively.
$FV=1600(1.05)^3+1600(1.05)^2+1600(1.05)$.
In increasing-power order, this geometric series has first term $1600(1.05)$, common ratio $1.05$ and three terms.
$FV=\dfrac{1600(1.05)(1.05^3-1)}{0.05}=\$5296.20$.

foundation.question_text:
An organization invests $\$5000$ at the beginning of each year for $6\text{ years}$ into a charity reserve earning $8\%$ p.a. compounded annually.
Calculate the future value at the end of the $6\text{ years}$, to the nearest cent.
foundation.solution_text:
$a = 5000$, $r = 0.08$, $n = 6$.
The six payments earn between one and six annual periods of interest.
$FV=5000(1.08)+5000(1.08)^2+\dots+5000(1.08)^6$.
The geometric series has first term $5000(1.08)$, common ratio $1.08$ and six terms.
$FV=\dfrac{5000(1.08)(1.08^6-1)}{0.08}$
$\approx\$39614.02$.

development.question_text:
On each birthday starting on her 1st birthday up to and including her 18th birthday ($18\text{ deposits}$), Chloe's parents deposit $\$400$ into an investment earning $6.5\%$ p.a. compounded annually.
No further deposits are made. Calculate the total in the account on her 19th birthday, to the nearest cent.
development.solution_text:
The valuation date is Chloe's 19th birthday. The deposit on her 1st birthday earns 18 years of interest, and the deposit on her 18th birthday earns one year.
$a=400$, $r=0.065$, $n=18$.
$FV=400(1.065)^{18}+400(1.065)^{17}+\dots+400(1.065)$.
In increasing-power order, this geometric series has first term $400(1.065)$, common ratio $1.065$ and 18 terms.
$FV=\dfrac{400(1.065)(1.065^{18}-1)}{0.065}$.
The balance to the nearest cent is $\$13\,806.69$.

development.question_text:
A tenant deposits $\$650$ at the beginning of each quarter into a sinking fund earning $5.6\%$ p.a. compounded quarterly for $7\text{ years}$.
Calculate the final balance of the fund at the end of the $7\text{ years}$, to the nearest cent.
development.solution_text:
$a=650$, $r=\dfrac{0.056}{4}=0.014$, $n=7\times4=28$.
The payment and compounding periods both last one quarter. The 28 deposits earn between one and 28 quarters of interest.
$FV=650(1.014)+650(1.014)^2+\dots+650(1.014)^{28}$.
The geometric series has first term $650(1.014)$, common ratio $1.014$ and 28 terms.
$FV=\dfrac{650(1.014)(1.014^{28}-1)}{0.014}$.
The balance to the nearest cent is $\$22\,405.62$.

development.question_text:
A club wants to have $\$45\,000$ in $5\text{ years}$ to renovate its clubhouse.
The committee plans to make equal contributions at the beginning of each month into an account earning $7.2\%$ p.a. compounded monthly.
Calculate the required monthly contribution, to the nearest cent.
development.solution_text:
$r=\dfrac{0.072}{12}=0.006$, $n=5\times12=60$.
Let the monthly contribution be $a$. The first contribution earns 60 months of interest and the final contribution earns one month.
$45000=a(1.006)+a(1.006)^2+\dots+a(1.006)^{60}$.
The geometric series has first term $a(1.006)$, common ratio $1.006$ and 60 terms.
$45000=a\dfrac{1.006(1.006^{60}-1)}{0.006}$.
The exact accumulation factor is $\dfrac{1.006(1.006^{60}-1)}{0.006}$.
The monthly contribution to the nearest cent is $\$621.58$.

development.question_text:
A small business invests $\$1200$ at the beginning of every $6\text{ months}$ for $8\text{ years}$ into a capital reserve fund earning $6.2\%$ p.a. compounded half-yearly.
Find the future value of the reserve fund at the end of the $8\text{ years}$, to the nearest cent.
development.solution_text:
$a=1200$, $r=\dfrac{0.062}{2}=0.031$, $n=8\times2=16$.
The payment and compounding periods both last six months. The 16 payments earn between one and 16 half-years of interest.
$FV=1200(1.031)+1200(1.031)^2+\dots+1200(1.031)^{16}$.
The geometric series has first term $1200(1.031)$, common ratio $1.031$ and 16 terms.
$FV=\dfrac{1200(1.031)(1.031^{16}-1)}{0.031}$.
The balance to the nearest cent is $\$25\,135.76$.

development.question_text:
A family sets a target of saving $\$60\,000$ in $6\text{ years}$ with equal start-of-year deposits earning $7.5\%$ p.a. compounded annually.
Find the required annual deposit, to the nearest cent.
development.solution_text:
$r=0.075$, $n=6$.
Let the annual deposit be $a$. At the end of year 6, the six deposits have earned between one and six years of interest.
$60000=a(1.075)+a(1.075)^2+\dots+a(1.075)^6$.
The geometric series has first term $a(1.075)$, common ratio $1.075$ and six terms.
$60000=a\dfrac{1.075(1.075^6-1)}{0.075}$.
The accumulation factor is exactly $7.787321867431640625$.
$a=\dfrac{60000}{7.787321867431640625}\approx\$7704.83$.

development.solution_text:

The first deposit earns 60 months of interest and the final deposit earns one month.
$FV=275(1.004)+275(1.004)^2+\dots+275(1.004)^{60}$.
The geometric series has first term $275(1.004)$, common ratio $1.004$ and 60 terms.

mastery.question_text: A company contributes $\$10\,000$ on 1st January each year ($n=20\text{ contributions}$) into a retirement scheme earning $8.5\%$ p.a. compounded annually. (a) Calculate the total value at the end of the 20th year, to the nearest cent. (b) Calculate, to the nearest cent, the annual contribution $M$ corresponding to a target fund value of $\$1\,000\,000$ at the end of the 20th year.
mastery.solution_text:
Part (a):
$a=10000$, $r=0.085$, $n=20$.
The contribution on 1 January of year 1 earns 20 years of interest; the contribution on 1 January of year 20 earns one year.
$FV=10000(1.085)+10000(1.085)^2+\dots+10000(1.085)^{20}$.
The geometric series has first term $10000(1.085)$, common ratio $1.085$ and 20 terms.
Let the exact accumulation factor be $F=\dfrac{1.085(1.085^{20}-1)}{0.085}$.
$FV=10000F$.
The balance to the nearest cent is $\$524\,890.59$.
Part (b):
$1000000=M(1.085)+M(1.085)^2+\dots+M(1.085)^{20}=MF$.
The annual contribution to the nearest cent is $\$19\,051.61$.
Use the exact factor $F$ for both parts. Rounding the contribution to cents generally makes the resulting balance slightly different from the exact target.

mastery.question_text:

Calculate the value of the account at the end of the $15\text{ years}$, to the nearest cent.
mastery.solution_text:
$r=0.066/12=0.0055$, $n=15\times12=180$.
The 180 start-of-month payments earn between one and 180 months of interest.
$FV=550(1.0055)+550(1.0055)^2+\dots+550(1.0055)^{180}$.
The geometric series has first term $550(1.0055)$, common ratio $1.0055$ and 180 terms.
$FV=\dfrac{550(1.0055)(1.0055^{180}-1)}{0.0055}$.
The balance to the nearest cent is $\$169\,320.55$.

mastery.question_text:
A scholarship fund receives $\$3000$ on 1st January every year for $12\text{ years}$ at $7\%$ p.a. compounded annually.
Show by geometric series derivation why the future value at the end of the 12th year is $FV = \dfrac{3000 \times 1.07 \times (1.07^{12}-1)}{0.07}$ and evaluate it to the nearest cent. Also calculate, to the nearest dollar, the amount to which the first deposit has grown at that date.
mastery.solution_text:
1. **Write the series of terms starting from $a(1+r)$ up to $a(1+r)^{n}$, checking that there are $n$ payments and that the final payment earns one period of interest.**
The first deposit made at the start of year 1 compounds for 12 years: $3000(1.07)^{12}$.
The final deposit made at the start of year 12 compounds for one year: $3000(1.07)$.
$FV=3000(1.07)+3000(1.07)^2+\dots+3000(1.07)^{12}$.
2. **Identify the first term and common ratio, derive the geometric-series sum, then evaluate using full precision and round as requested.**
The first term is $3000(1.07)$, the common ratio is $1.07$ and there are 12 terms.
$FV=\dfrac{3000(1.07)(1.07^{12}-1)}{1.07-1}\approx\$57421.07$.
The first deposit alone has grown to $3000(1.07)^{12}\approx\$6756.57$, or $\$6757$ to the nearest dollar.
